claims.value: Plotho describes the early French covering force as about two battalions, three cavalry regiments and four guns, followed by another column of about twelve battalions/two batteries. These are different retreating components, not complete headcounts; Vaudoncourt assigns the final town defense to Teste without artillery.
claims.rationale: Component unit counts and successive roles, not a complete French strength or an invented unit-to-people conversion. English rendering (ours): "About two battalions, three cavalry regiments and four guns; another column of about twelve battalions and two batteries. Teste was left no artillery."

claims.value: Plotho places Vandamme in charge of holding Namur while Grouchy departed with the fourth corps; Vaudoncourt assigns the town’s final defense and evacuation to Teste. Pirch I directed the pursuit/attacks, with Sohr as advance guard.
claims.rationale: Superior versus local/rear-guard assignments retained, no automatic contradiction or equal army-wide attribution. English rendering (ours): "Vandamme had to defend Namur; Teste’s division was charged with it; Pirch ordered the movement."

claims.value: Plotho describes French departure and Prussian occupation at the end; Vaudoncourt describes Teste withdrawing after the evacuation was complete. Neither changes Bodart’s frozen Prussian winner.
claims.rationale: Town possession and successful covering withdrawal can coexist; no automatic winner reversal or campaign credit. English rendering (ours): "Namur was occupied by the Prussians; then, everything having been evacuated, Teste left Namur."
